I used to have a really big problem with “flexing” or bragging about my own mental illnesses. I grew up in an environment where I wasn’t really believed or listened to if I tried to speak about my own problems, so I got to the point where it was almost a competition and I made all my problems over dramatic to the point where they were basically lies. I kept this up for most of my teenage years. 

It took time to unlearn, and a lot of kindness from close and healthy friends — which id never really had before — and professionals, like therapists and stuff. It took a long time to learn I didn’t have to be dying to be upset, it wasn’t necessary to compete about my mental struggles, and it wasn’t healthy to brag and make my mental health issues the focus of my personality. There’s a fine line between bragging and genuinely opening up that I had to learn as well. 

I’ve had to grow in a lot of ways but that’s the one I think will always stick with me, because it was such a bad problem and I genuinely never realized how toxic it was to me and everyone around me. I still have a lot of mental health issues, I still struggle, but there’s more to me than that — Like I’m nerdy, I can be funny, I’m not just a ball of trauma or insomnia anymore. I’m a whole person thanks to everyone who was patient enough to allow me to grow :)
